title: A numerically evaluated area

title: Reading information from a derivative graph
subtopic: Graphs of f and its derivatives

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the x-coordinates of the local maximum and minimum of f, justifying each.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of the point of inflexion of f.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why the graph alone does not determine the y-coordinates of these points on f.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: State where f is concave up.

steps.text: At $x=-1$, $f^\prime$ changes from positive to negative.
f has a local maximum at $x=-1$.
At $x=1$, $f^\prime$ changes from negative to positive.
f has a local minimum at $x=1$.
Adding any constant to f leaves its derivative unchanged, so the vertical position of f is not specified.

verification.method: Independent symbolic/numeric and mathematical reasoning checks
verification.notes: Displayed parameters were recalculated; see the per-record AA SL author-review ledger. First-derivative sign chart and second-derivative sign change checked; derivative ordinate is not mistaken for f ordinate.
